heading: SEBI's Mutual Fund-Only PMS: A New Era for Wealth Advisers?
tldr: SEBI has proposed a new framework for Portfolio Management Services (PMS) focused exclusively on mutual funds.
This initiative aims to make professional portfolio management more accessible to a broader base of investors.
Financial advisers, including Mutual Fund Distributors (MFDs) and Registered Investment Advisers (RIAs), could manage client portfolios and charge direct fees.
The proposal includes a reduced minimum investment threshold of ₹25 lakh and a lower net worth requirement for providers.
Despite simplified norms, significant compliance demands and operational complexities may still challenge smaller advisory firms.
caption:
Ever wondered if professional money management could be simpler and more accessible? SEBI is thinking along similar lines! They've proposed a new way for experts to manage your money using only mutual funds, possibly with lower investment amounts. This could be a game-changer for many, making it easier to get tailored financial advice. Intrigued? Read more about what this could mean for your investments.
